name: straus_cofactor_residue_class

phase_0.boundary_condition: The terminal anchor TANCH is the residue lattice modulo r and small primes, which contains the entire decision structure: all input residue data, the congruence test, and the exhibited divisor are bounded within this modular arithmetic closure.

VINIT.chosen_element: The empty residue register before any prime data is loaded
VINIT.justification: Before the odd integer n congruent to 1 modulo 24 and the parameter r congruent to 3 modulo 4 are introduced, no residue data exists. The system begins in the void state with no primes, no residues, and no divisor candidate.

TANCH.chosen_element: The residue lattice modulo r and small primes
TANCH.justification: This lattice forms the closed boundary that contains the entire decision structure. Every residue condition, every congruence test, and every divisor exhibition is bounded within this modular arithmetic closure, making it the terminal anchor of the system.

AFWD.chosen_element: Forward propagation of residue data through the lattice
AFWD.justification: The forward morphism carries residue data from the input primes dividing r and small primes toward the congruence test. This is the directed transformation that moves the system from raw residue data to a decision about the existence of a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r.

AREV.chosen_element: Reverse descent from the congruence test back to divisor exhibition
AREV.justification: The reverse morphism descends from the decision state back to the explicit construction of the divisor. When the congruence test succeeds, the system reverses direction to exhibit the actual divisor that satisfies the congruence, moving from abstract residue data to concrete divisor output.

CLINK.chosen_element: Sequential composition of residue loading, congruence testing, and divisor exhibition
CLINK.justification: The composition operator chains the three phases of the decision structure: first loading residue data at primes dividing r and small primes, then testing the congruence condition, and finally exhibiting the divisor when it exists. Each phase is linked in sequence.

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: Self-referential residue data that validates its own congruence
IMSCRIB.justification: The identity token represents the self-recognition property of the residue data: the residue data at primes dividing r and small primes is sufficient to determine the divisor without external search. The system recognizes itself in its own residue structure.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: The decision fork that splits residue data into congruence-satisfying and congruence-violating branches
FSPLIT.justification: The FSPLIT divides the residue data into two arms: the T-arm where the congruence condition n(n+r)/4 congruent to 0 modulo some divisor congruent to -1 modulo r is satisfied, and the F-arm where no such divisor exists. This is the fundamental branching point of the decision structure.

FFUSE.chosen_element: The rejoining of the congruence test result into a single decision state
FFUSE.justification: The FFUSE reunites the two arms of the decision fork. The T-arm carries the affirmative result with the exhibited divisor, and the F-arm carries the negative result with no divisor. They rejoin into a single B4 verdict over the residue lattice.

EVALT.chosen_element: The affirmative state where a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r is found and exhibited
EVALT.justification: The EVALT anchors the T-arm of the decision fork. When the residue data at primes dividing r and small primes confirms the existence of a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r, this token marks the constructive proof and the exhibition of that divisor.

EVALF.chosen_element: The negative state where no divisor congruent to -1 modulo r exists
EVALF.justification: The EVALF anchors the F-arm of the decision fork. When the residue data at primes dividing r and small primes refutes the existence of a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r, this token marks the constructive refutation.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: The paradice state where residue data simultaneously supports and refutes the divisor existence
ENGAGR.justification: The ENGAGR represents a contradiction held live: the residue data at some primes dividing r and small primes may simultaneously indicate both the presence and absence of a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r. This is a legitimate B-state, not an error.

IFIX.chosen_element: The permanent record of the exhibited divisor and its congruence
IFIX.justification: The IFIX token creates an append-only, irreversible record of the divisor that was found and the congruence it satisfies. This is the final output of the decision structure, fixed permanently in the residue lattice.

phase_2.split_element: The decision fork that tests whether n(n+r)/4 admits a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r
phase_2.split_input: The residue data of the odd integer n congruent to 1 modulo 24 at primes dividing r and at small primes, together with the parameter r congruent to 3 modulo 4
split_outputs: The T-arm: residue data confirming the existence of a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r, leading to divisor exhibition
The F-arm: residue data refuting the existence of such a divisor, leading to negative conclusion
phase_2.fuse_element: The FFUSE that reunites the congruence test result into a single decision state over the residue lattice
phase_2.fuse_result: A single B4 verdict over the residue lattice modulo r and small primes, which may be T (divisor found), F (no divisor), or B (contradiction held live)
phase_2.failure_reason: Tri-ancestral reconnection over a transformed object — closes

phase_3.void_description: The uninitialized state before any residue data is loaded: no primes dividing r, no small primes, no residue values, and no divisor candidate. The register holds 00.
phase_3.true_description: The affirmative state where the residue data at primes dividing r and small primes confirms the existence of a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r, and that divisor has been exhibited. The register holds 01.
phase_3.false_description: The negative state where the residue data at primes dividing r and small primes refutes the existence of any divisor congruent to -1 modulo r. The register holds 10.
phase_3.both_description: The paradice state where the residue data simultaneously supports and refutes the existence of a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r, holding both states without resolution. The register holds 11.

steps.domain_action: The system begins in the void state with no residue data loaded, no primes identified, and no divisor candidate established.
The residue lattice modulo r and small primes is established as the terminal anchor that bounds the entire decision structure.
The forward morphism loads residue data of the odd integer n congruent to 1 modulo 24 at primes dividing r and at small primes, propagating this data toward the congruence test.
The decision fork splits the residue data into two arms: the T-arm where a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r may exist, and the F-arm where no such divisor exists.
The T-arm is anchored by the affirmative evaluation, confirming that the residue data supports the existence of a divisor congruent to -1 modulo r.
The reverse morphism descends from the congruence test result back to the explicit construction of the divisor, moving from abstract residue data to concrete divisor output.
The permanent record of the exhibited divisor and its congruence is fixed in an append-only, irreversible register within the residue lattice.
The F-arm is anchored by the negative evaluation, confirming that the residue data refutes the existence of any divisor congruent to -1 modulo r.
A paradice state is entered where the residue data simultaneously supports and refutes the divisor existence, holding both states without resolution.
The two arms of the decision fork rejoin into a single B4 verdict over the residue lattice, with conflicting arms fusing to B.
The sequential composition chains the residue loading, congruence testing, and divisor exhibition phases into a single coherent decision structure.
The self-referential identity confirms that the residue data at primes dividing r and small primes is sufficient to determine the divisor without external search, closing the loop.

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The compiler translates the residue data of n at primes dividing r and small primes into congruence test operations over the modular arithmetic lattice, mapping each residue condition to a logical gate in the decision structure.
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: Components communicate through the residue lattice modulo r and small primes, passing residue data from the input phase to the congruence test phase and then to the divisor exhibition phase via directed morphisms.
phase_5.memory_mechanism: State is stored in the residue lattice as a register of Belnap values (N, T, F, B) at each prime dividing r and small prime, with the IFIX token creating permanent append-only records of exhibited divisors.
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The scheduler determines the order of operations by the structure of the residue lattice: residue data is loaded first, then the decision fork is evaluated, then the arms are processed in parallel, and finally the results are fused.
phase_5.alfs_store: The canonical reference is the residue lattice modulo r and small primes, which serves as the bootstrap store for all congruence tests and divisor exhibitions in this domain.

phase_6.cycle_cost: Each operation cycle consumes computational work proportional to the number of primes dividing r and small primes, as each residue condition must be evaluated and propagated through the lattice.
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: Before the cycle, the residue register is in a state of partial evaluation with some residue data loaded but no congruence test completed and no divisor exhibited.
phase_6.post_cycle_state: After the cycle, the residue register holds a resolved B4 verdict (T, F, or B) over the residue lattice, with the divisor either exhibited and fixed or the negative conclusion recorded.
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The cycle is entropy-conservative because the residue data is neither created nor destroyed; it is only reorganized from raw input form into a resolved decision state, with the IFIX token preserving the exhibited divisor as a permanent record.
